entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15480"/><div sID="gen29831" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15480"/><hi type="bold">3-10. Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came first to the sepulchre--</hi>These particulars have a singular air of artless truth about them. Mary, in her grief, runs to the two apostles who were soon to be so closely associated in proclaiming the Saviour's resurrection, and they, followed by Mary, hasten to see with their own eyes. The younger disciple outruns the older; love haply supplying swifter wings. He stoops, he gazes in, but enters not the open sepulchre, held back probably by a reverential fear. The bolder Peter, coming up, goes in at once, and is rewarded with bright evidence of what had happened. <div eID="gen29831" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15484"/><div sID="gen29840" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15484"/><hi type="bold">11-15. But Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping, &c.--</hi>Brief was the stay of those two men. But Mary, arriving perhaps by another direction after they left, lingers at the spot, weeping for her missing Lord. As she gazes through her tears on the open tomb, she also ventures to stoop down and look into it, when lo! "two angels in white" (as from the world of light, and see on <reference osisRef="Matt.28.3">Mt 28:3</reference>) appear to her in a "sitting" posture, "as having finished some business, and awaiting some one to impart tidings to" [Bengel]. <div eID="gen29840" type="x-p"/>

Jesus saith unto her, Mary--</hi>It is not now the distant, though respectful, "Woman." entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15491"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="John.20.19-John.20.23">Joh 20:19-23</reference>. Jesus Appears to the Assembled Disciples.</title> <div sID="gen29852" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15491"/><hi type="bold">19-23. the same day at evening, the first day of the week, the doors being shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus--</hi>plainly not by the ordinary way of entrance.<div eID="gen29852" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29853" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and saith unto them Peace be unto you--</hi>not the mere wish that even His own exalted peace might be theirs (<reference osisRef="John.14.27">Joh 14:27</reference>), but conveying it into their hearts, even as He "opened their understandings to understand the scriptures" (<reference osisRef="Luke.24.45">Lu 24:45</reference>). <div eID="gen29853" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: Joh 20:19-23 . Jesus Appears to the Assembled Disciples. 19-23. the same day at evening, the first day of the week, the doors being shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus-- plainly not by the ordinary way of entrance. and saith unto them Peace be unto you-- not the mere wish that even His own exalted peace might be theirs ( Joh 14:27 ), but conveying it into their hearts, even as He "opened their understandings to understand the scriptures" ( Lu 24:45 ).
